references.text: Israel was forbidden to make a covenant with the Canaanites and their gods, which the Gibeonites tricked Joshua into doing
God's command not to make a covenant with the peoples of Canaan, contrasting with the covenant Joshua made with the Gibeonites
The law requiring an offer of peace to cities far away before attacking, which the Gibeonites exploited by pretending they came from a distant land
Saul broke this covenant with the Gibeonites, leading to a famine in David's time, demonstrating the binding power of covenants
The law that an oath to the Lord must be kept and not broken, explaining why Joshua honored the covenant with the Gibeonites
A warning against breaking covenants and oaths, highlighting the importance of keeping promises even to enemies
